claim: A compact set of MLP blocks and attention heads in middle-to-late layers writes the confidence-inflation signal at the final token for verbalized confidence in two 3B instruct models.
stance_target: causal/mechanistic evidence on verbalized confidence exists outside code
quoted_support: we find that a compact set of MLP blocks and attention heads, concentrated in middle-to-late layers, consistently writes the confidence-inflation signal at the final token position.

breadth.confidence_families: verbalized integer confidence 0-99 after answer (two-step elicitation, Fig 1, Sec 2); internal logit-gap proxy TSLD
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; scale check on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Sec 2, Appendix A)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: base model, instruct comparison; only instruct models)
breadth.elicitation_formats: one format: verbalized 0-99 integer after the model's own factual answer (Fig 1)
breadth.benchmarks: PopQA, NQOpen, MMLU (factual QA); no code benchmark
breadth.label_source: factual answer correctness against dataset gold answers
breadth.label_independence: dataset gold labels, independent of model
breadth.calibration_metrics: ECE and Brier before/after intervention (Table 3); TSLD
breadth.granularity: per-question final token position; circuit components (MLP blocks, attention heads)
breadth.causal_intervention: yes: edge attribution patching with integrated gradients, mean ablation, activation steering; circuit completeness 74-79% (Table 2); steering lowers ECE (Table 3)

claim: Steering or ablation on the discovered circuit substantially lowers ECE of verbalized confidence.
stance_target: causal interventions on the confidence readout improve calibration
scope_conditions: factual QA only; Table 3 and scale check on Qwen2.5-7B
quoted_support: steering on this circuit reduces ECE from 0.647 to 0.068 on PopQA
